questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Right triangles ABC and DEF have right angles at C and F and ∠A ≅ ∠D. Explain why BC/AB = EF/DE.
questions.prompt_markup: Right triangles ABC and DEF have right angles at C and F and ∠A ≅ ∠D. Explain why BC/AB = EF/DE.
questions.required_method: Use AA similarity, then the proportion of corresponding sides, rearranged.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: right angles and ∠A ≅ ∠D give AA similarity; BC/EF = AB/DE; rearranging gives BC/AB = EF/DE. So the ratio depends only on the angle.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has the right angle at C, AC = 4 and BC = 3. Right triangle DEF has the right angle at F, ∠D ≅ ∠A and DE = 20. Find EF and DF, and explain why tan A = tan D.
questions.prompt_markup: Right triangle ABC has the right angle at C, AC = 4 and BC = 3. Right triangle DEF has the right angle at F, ∠D ≅ ∠A and DE = 20. Find EF and DF, and explain why tan A = tan D.
questions.correct_answer: AB = 5 and the triangles are similar (AA) with factor 4, so EF = 12 and DF = 16; tan A = 3/4 and tan D = 12/16 = 3/4, equal because corresponding sides are proportional.
